title: Makerspace Network — Achievement definition
description: A unit of TRANSFERABLE competence. Published by the network at a stable versioned URL, aligned to by each space's own local badge via Open Badges 3.0 Achievement.alignment. Site-specific knowledge is deliberately NOT here — see docs/ACHIEVEMENTS.md for why the split is the whole design.

version.description: Never mutate a published version. Credentials are signed against it and must keep meaning what they meant.

hazard_class.description: The boundary that decides granularity. One achievement per hazard profile, not per brand and not per shop. If two machines can hurt you the same ways, they share an achievement.

extends.description: For extension achievements: the core achievement they build on, e.g. 'table-saw-operator/v1'.

competencies.description: The checklist. Each item must be independently assessable and must be TRUE AT ANY SPACE — if it depends on this shop's layout, rules, or equipment, it belongs in site_specific instead.

statement.description: What the holder can do or knows. Written so a shop manager can say yes or no.

min_assessment.description: The weakest method that may be claimed for this item. A video alone does not assess a psychomotor skill.

critical.description: An item whose absence makes the whole credential unsafe to honour. A local badge missing a critical item cannot claim alignment.

excludes.description: Operations explicitly NOT covered. Stating these is what stops scope creep and stops a receiving space assuming more than was assessed.

site_specific.description: Knowledge that does NOT transfer and must be delivered locally regardless of what credential the person arrives with. The credential substitutes for the competence assessment, never for the local orientation.

brand_deltas.description: Where a specific machine adds knowledge on top of the generic competence. A holder trained on one may need a short addendum at a space using another — an addendum, not another badge.

adds.description: What this machine requires beyond the core competencies.

asymmetry.description: Where training on this machine may LEAVE A GAP against the generic competence rather than adding to it. The dangerous direction — see docs/ACHIEVEMENTS.md §4.

capability.description: The Capability vocabulary value this achievement authorises against.

authors.description: Which spaces co-authored this. A definition written by one space is a draft, not a standard.
